config.note: Test 2: the four scored drafts joined and padded to 18,007 characters, sent in windows as the app does.

findings.note: "realization" buries the act of realizing behind the empty verb "come to".
"Determination" names the act of deciding, while "makes" carries no meaning. The action is buried in the noun.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: "decision" and "evaluation" both bury their verbs; the first is carried by "was made" and the second by "carried out".
"evaluation" is the action; "carried out" does the work of a verb that "evaluate" would do.
"Decision" names the act of deciding, carried by the empty verb "made"; the actor Ellen is preserved in the clause.
The noun "undertaking" buries the act of undertaking, carried by the empty verb "given".
The noun "assessment" buries the act of assessing, carried by the empty verb "carry out".
The noun "review" buries the verb "review" behind the empty verb "conduct".
"There was" carries the action noun "expectation"; the verb "expect" is buried.
"Made" is an empty verb carrying the noun "observation"; the verb "observe" is buried.
"determination" names the act of determining, and its verb "make" does no work. Combined with "was decided" in the same sentence, the actor behind both actions is absent.
"Decision" carries the action while "would be made" supplies only the tense.
The clause names no one who should note this, and the surrounding sentences do not supply a noter. The missing actor is whoever the draft wants to require this acknowledgment of.
The draft never says who raised the concerns, though the surrounding sentences point to unnamed people. The actor is hidden.
The draft does not say who decided that all changes would go through this process. The surrounding sentences describe the board's current schedule, not who made this rule.

findings.quote: The combination was forgotten twice in the first week
findings.note: The draft does not name who forgot the combination, though the surrounding sentences about buying the lock and walking make the author the likely actor.
The draft never says who should note this. The framing of the eleven-change figure as worth noting is left unattributed.
The draft never says who failed to issue the warnings. Responsibility for the warning sits with some body, and the text withholds it.
No one is named as having made the promise of sandbags. The paragraph leaves the acting party unidentified.

findings.quote: By the time I reached the top of the hill that February,
findings.note: The subject is preceded by 12 words before "I": "By the time I reached the top of the hill that February,".
"The board" opens four consecutive sentences (meets, makes, then posts, and the earlier sentence). This is a run of four sentences with the same two opening words.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: The subject Ellen is preceded by 25 words of introductory material.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: Eighteen words precede the main subject "I", which is delayed by a long introductory participial phrase.
Doubled pair saying one thing twice: "plain and simple".
"picturesque" appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in the phrase "a picturesque row of Victorian houses".
"cumbersome" repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in "Its checklist is cumbersome for a one-line fix".

findings.quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences open with the same subject-verb template, "I" plus a past-tense verb, adding only a sequence of times.
Doubled pair: "full and complete" says one thing twice.
Doubled pair: "each and every" says the same thing twice.
"Both" opens three consecutive sentences ("Both return", "Both filter", "Both start"), the same template with no gain from the repetition.
"decision" repeats the root of "decided" from the opening of the same sentence, which also uses the same passive construction.

"resolution" is repeated within two sentences; it first appears in the preceding sentence in the phrase "a resolution would be arrived at". The phrase "was arrived at" also repeats from that sentence.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: "feeling" appears three times within three sentences, and the two closing sentences share the template "It is a feeling that ...". The first occurrence is "with the feeling that nothing had been accomplished".
"no" is used three times within three sentences: "no Accept button", "no apply action" and "has no replacement field". The earlier occurrences are in the two preceding sentences.

findings.quote: A monthly bus pass costs sixty.
findings.note: The sentence opens on a new element, the bus pass, which nothing earlier in the paragraph prepared. The previous sentence was about annual car costs.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city
findings.note: The previous sentence ends on wet socks and a temper, and the only link to the new subject is the shared idea of snow and winter. The sentence opens on municipal snow contracts, an element nothing earlier in the paragraph introduced.

findings.quote: Concerns have been raised about the delays for over a year.
findings.note: The opening introduces unnamed "Concerns" as a new element; the previous sentence is about the board's checklist and weekly schedule. The link to the delays appears only at the end of the sentence.

findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June.
findings.note: The sentence opens on a bike, which the paragraph has not mentioned; the previous sentence was about crossing a bridge on foot versus by car.

findings.quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature
findings.note: The sentence opens on a general fact about gluten development, which nothing in the paragraph has prepared. The sentence before was about Tom driving for flour.

findings.quote: The hall kitchen is very small, and only one oven works.
findings.note: The opening introduces the hall kitchen, which the previous sentence mentions only at its end as the location of the trestle table.

findings.quote: The flood wall was built in 1962
findings.note: The previous sentence is about the street being closed by police; the flood wall is a new element that nothing earlier in the paragraph prepared.

findings.quote: She went back for a tray of sourdough starter
findings.note: The sentence opens on a new item, the sourdough starter tray, after the previous sentence was about carrying the cash box and order book to the flat. The starter has not appeared before, so the reader meets it only as the sentence develops.

findings.quote: Approvals are logged automatically by the deploy tool,
findings.note: The opening introduces automatic logging by the deploy tool, an element not prepared by the previous sentence about the pilot period and limited evidence.
The A/B judge appears with no prior mention; the preceding sentences are about the schema and the system preamble. The link to the preamble arrives only at the end, in "forbids it".
The opening element "the stack" is new; the preceding sentence was about the feature list and the two rules, with no stack mentioned earlier in the paragraph.

The sentence opens on "Rust", a new element; the previous sentence was about Tauri wrapping the editor layer. The link to Tauri is only recoverable from the pronoun "them" earlier, not from where this sentence begins.

findings.quote: Packaging and notarising a BEAM app on macOS is more work than tauri build.
findings.note: The sentence opens on "Packaging and notarising", a new element; the previous sentence was about OTP's runtime strengths under load. Nothing earlier in the paragraph prepared packaging or notarising as a topic.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Empty figure: the vehicle of the toll booth supplies no mechanism or comparison beyond the delay already stated, and it sits inside a paragraph that names a bottleneck and missed deadlines literally, so the image adds nothing the literal claim does not.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored
findings.note: Mixed figure: the cocoon image and the anchor-and-mooring image appear in the same sentence and cannot both hold of the same thing. The draft never settles which picture of the car it wants.

findings.quote: the city opened up like a book
findings.note: Empty figure. The simile supplies no mechanism or picture beyond the claim that walking changed how the writer sees the neighbourhood, which the surrounding sentences already state plainly.

findings.quote: a straitjacket that ties every team to the same Thursday
findings.note: Mixed figure. The sentence holds two incompatible images within its span: a net that catches and a garment that ties, and a straitjacket does not tie its wearer to a day of the week.

findings.quote: the beating heart of Quay Street
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the claim that the bakery matters to the street; the draft leaves the actual role the bakery plays unstated.

findings.quote: the flood was a wake-up call
findings.note: Stock image. The paragraph never states what the street is being woken to or what changed for it, so the cliché carries the claim by itself.
